chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father, and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, both together from Ibn Abi Najran, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) ruled regarding four who had drunk (wine) and became intoxicated. They then took weapons against each other and fought, so two were killed and two were wounded.

He ordered the two wounded to each be flogged eighty lashes, and ruled that the blood-money for the two killed be borne by the two wounded. He also ordered that the injuries of the two wounded be assessed and deducted from the blood-money. If the two wounded then die, there is nothing owed by anyone from among the guardians of the two killed.

key_terms.الْمَجْرُوحَيْنِ: The two wounded ones; dual form indicating both injured parties
key_terms.جَلْدَة: A lash or stroke of the whip; the prescribed hadd punishment for wine-drinking is eighty lashes
key_terms.دِيَة: Blood-money (diya): the mandatory financial compensation paid to the victim's family in lieu of retaliatory punishment
key_terms.قَضَى: He ruled/judged; used for authoritative judicial pronouncements by the Imam

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali rule regarding four men who got drunk, fought with weapons, and two were killed?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) reports a ruling of Imam Ali (AS) concerning four men who drank wine, became intoxicated, armed themselves, and fought: two were killed and two wounded. Ali's judgment applied three penalties simultaneously — each of the two wounded received eighty lashes for the hadd of wine-drinking, was made liable for the blood-money of the two killed, and had their own wound-compensation deducted from that blood-money. The ruling reflects early Islamic jurisprudence's principle that one who commits a crime while intoxicated remains fully liable, and introduces the principle of wound-deduction (qisas al-jurh) to avoid double compensation.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim from his father, and Muhammad Bin Yahya from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, both together from Ibn Abu Najran, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Muhammad Bin Qays, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Amir Al-Momineen<sup>asws</sup> judged regarding four who had drunk (wine) so they were intoxicated. So they took weapons upon each other and fought. So two were killed and two were wounded.

So he<sup>asws</sup> ordered for the two injured ones, so each one of them were whipped eighty lashes, and judged with regards to the wergild of the two killed ones to be upon the two injured ones, and ordered that surgery be performed on the injuries, so it was reimbursed from the wergild. So if the two injured ones died, so there would be nothing upon anyone from the guardians of the two killed ones’.
